title: DNR Summer Courses
content:
Last summer, we launched a new and experimental education program. Instructor facilitated a DNR Bootcamp whose waitlist and level of interest far exceeded our expectations. Last fall, we expanded this program by offering an additional Technology Criticism course with , author of Against Platforms (2025).

This summer we are adding “Contemporary Art History” with artist and educator Andy Bennentt, who alongside Harris Rosenblum has facilitated internal art critique groups for the DNR discord community over the last two years.

After five years of independent reading groups, crit groups, film screenings, and more, we are taking on the task of educating the next cohort of artists and creatives. You can enroll today: view all DNR Spring 2026 courses here.

Subscribe now

All courses will take place on Discord. Students must be prompt in responding to onboarding emails and be prepared to use the platform.

Summer Bootcamp (Sundays)

INSTRUCTOR:
DATES: Sundays, 8/9, 8/16, 8/23, & 8/30
TIME: 1:00 - 3:00pm EST

Four week intensive course delving into the core ideas and questions explored in the foundational stages of DNR. We will examine artworks, texts, and online media covering topics: internet-informed identity, political futures, & post-internet art. Facilitated by artist Theresa Tomi Faison via Discord.

Enrollment is open today.

Summer Bootcamp (Mondays)

INSTRUCTOR:
DATES: Mondays, 8/10, 8/17, 8/24, & 8/31
TIME: 6:30 - 8:30pm EST

Four week intensive course delving into the core ideas and questions explored in the foundational stages of DNR. We will examine artworks, texts, and online media covering topics: internet-informed identity, political futures, & post-internet art. Facilitated by artist Theresa Tomi Faison via Discord.

Enrollment is open now.

Contemporary Art History

INSTRUCTOR: Andy Bennett
DATES: Tuesday, 8/11, 8/18, 8/25, 9/1
TIME: 6:30 - 8:30pm EST

This four-week course introduces students to ideas, artists, and debates in contemporary art through close readings of artworks, essays, and videos.The course is organized around four thematic problems that have reshaped artistic practice over the last fifty years: the relationship between art and life, the changing status of images, the materiality of moving images, and contemporary developments beyond post-internet art.

Enrollment is open today. Space is limited.

Find all DNR Fall courses here.

“The materials covered in the course clearly explicate our current political and institutional stagnation and decay, and through discussion provide possible ways forward. In addition to politically grounded texts, Tomi’s careful curation of artworks shown in class highlights artists reacting to, and not escaping from, our current cultural realities. This class is highly relevant to anyone interested in ultra-contemporary art, our psycho-political moment, and how those intersect. It was a privilege being a member of the first cohort; I cannot recommend it enough.”

— Nate De La Cruz, former student from DNR Summer 25: Bootcamp
